title: Leading Team Members Who Retire Before Retiring
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note names a phenomenon common in large, tenured organizations: senior team members who psychologically check out and coast for months or years before their actual retirement date, quietly dragging down team morale and productivity. Rather than accepting this as inevitable, the piece recommends actively re-engaging these team members with meaty, milestone-driven assignments that draw on their accumulated skills, and suggests that a change of scenery -- a new team or location -- can also help reignite commitment. It puts the onus squarely on leaders to identify disengagement honestly rather than quietly tolerating it.
points: Some senior team members effectively 'retire before retiring,' disengaging years ahead of their actual exit.
This quiet disengagement drags down team productivity and morale, but is often ignored to avoid conflict.
The remedy recommended is assigning meaty, milestone-based projects that use these team members' accumulated skills.
A change of team, division, or location is suggested as a way to reenergize disengaged senior staff.
Leaders are challenged to honestly identify who on their team has already 'retired' before their departure date.
quotes: The dirty secret everyone knows is that some leaders and team members retire before retiring.
Even though they have a tremendous amount to offer, these team members sit on their hands, stay below the radar, and dial back their contributions while they wait until retirement actually occurs.
Promoting more engagement with those who have lost their initiative begins with designing challenging assignments that utilize many of the skills these team members have developed over their careers.
Relocating the team member to a new team, division, or location may be just what they need to start fresh and deliver on the high expectations set by the leader.
The best leaders never accept anything but full engagement, especially from those who have the skills, wisdom, and experience to contribute.
